key_insight: Composition anisotropy in 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics enables an unusually large bulk photovoltaic field along the vertical nonpolar direction, far exceeding the in-plane polar response.
engineering_relevance: This points to a new design route for voltage-readout photodetectors and other optoelectronic devices that exploit strong, direction-dependent photovoltage in ferroelectric materials.
method: Analyzed bulk photovoltaic effect behavior in 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics.
Linked the response to shift-current physics and coupling between inorganic photoactive and organic insulating layers.
Derived formulas for laser-intensity and thickness-dependent photovoltage behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to two orders of magnitude higher vertical photovoltage than the polar in-plane direction and the highest BPE response among reported 2D HPFs.
watch_item: The effect is highly anisotropic and may be sensitive to composition, dimensional scaling, and device orientation, so implementation will require careful crystal and layer alignment.
paper_title: Composition Anisotropy Drives Large Bulk Photovoltaic Fields Along the Non-polar Vertical Direction in 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectrics
